mcqs.prompt: A security administrator wants to ensure that if a laptop is stolen, the data on the drive cannot be read. Which security measure addresses this concern?
mcqs.context: A stolen laptop's drive data must be unreadable.

options.rationale: Full-disk encryption renders the drive unreadable without the key — the direct protection against theft.
A screen lock delays access but does not protect the drive from removal and offline analysis.
A filter limits viewing angles; it does not protect stored data.
A cable lock deters theft of the device but does not protect data once stolen.

mcqs.explanation: Full-disk encryption (BitLocker with TPM) encrypts all drive contents so stolen media is unreadable. Screen locks and cable locks deter access but do not protect the data itself.

mcqs.prompt: An organization requires employees to provide a password AND a one-time code from an authenticator app to log in. Which security concept is being implemented?
mcqs.context: Login requires a password plus a one-time code from an authenticator app.

options.rationale: MFA combines two different factors — knowledge (password) and possession (the authenticator app) — as required here.
SSO lets one login reach many apps; it does not add a second factor.
RBAC assigns permissions by role; it is not an authentication method.
Least privilege limits permissions; unrelated to how users authenticate.

mcqs.explanation: MFA requires two or more factors from different categories: something you know (password), have (authenticator app code), or are (biometric). Password + one-time code is classic MFA.

mcqs.prompt: A technician is securing a server room and needs a control that PREVENTS unauthorized people from entering while someone else is let in. Which physical control addresses tailgating?
mcqs.context: A server room needs protection against tailgating.

options.rationale: A mantrap has two interlocked doors, so only one person can enter per credential use — the direct tailgating defense.
CCTV records incidents but does not prevent tailgating.
Privacy screens protect displays, not doorways.
Surge suppressors protect power, not physical access.

mcqs.explanation: A mantrap (access control vestibule) uses two doors that cannot both open at once, forcing one-person-per-authentication and blocking tailgating. CCTV is detective, not preventive.

mcqs.prompt: An administrator needs to restrict a finance user so they can access ONLY the accounting application and nothing else on their workstation. Which logical access concept applies?
mcqs.context: A finance user should access only the accounting app.

options.rationale: Least privilege grants only the minimum permissions needed — the accounting app and nothing more.
Encryption protects data at rest; it does not restrict which apps a user runs.
MFA strengthens authentication but does not limit access scope.
Screen locks protect an unattended session; they do not scope permissions.

mcqs.explanation: Least privilege gives users only the access their job requires. Restricting the finance user to the accounting app is a textbook least-privilege implementation.

mcqs.prompt: A user's Windows PC is running slowly and shows frequent pop-up ads. Which Windows built-in component provides real-time virus and threat protection?
mcqs.context: A Windows PC shows ad pop-ups and runs slowly; built-in protection is needed.

options.rationale: Windows Security includes Defender Antivirus real-time protection, firewall, and threat history — the built-in tool to scan and clean.
Task Manager shows processes but does not remove malware.
Disk Management handles partitions, not threats.
Registry Editor edits configuration; it is not a security scanner.

mcqs.explanation: Windows Security (formerly Windows Defender) provides real-time antivirus, firewall, and app/browser controls. The pop-ups suggest adware, which Defender can scan for and remove.

mcqs.prompt: A technician configures a Windows firewall rule that allows a specific application to accept inbound connections. What type of rule is this?
mcqs.context: A firewall rule allows one application to accept inbound traffic.

options.rationale: An application exception permits a specific program through the firewall — exactly what was configured.
Profiles (Domain/Private/Public) group rules by network type; they are not the rule itself.
Port forwarding is a router NAT function, not a Windows firewall app rule.
Group policy enforces settings; the firewall rule here is an app exception.

mcqs.explanation: Windows Defender Firewall uses application exceptions (app-based rules) to allow or block specific programs. Port-based rules and profiles are separate concepts.

mcqs.prompt: An organization centralizes user accounts, passwords, and Group Policy in a directory so users can log in to any domain computer. Which technology provides this?
mcqs.context: Centralized accounts and Group Policy across domain computers.

options.rationale: Active Directory centralizes accounts, authentication, and Group Policy for domain-joined computers.
Defender is antivirus/firewall, not a directory service.
BitLocker encrypts drives.
UAC prompts for elevation; it does not centralize accounts.

mcqs.explanation: Active Directory (AD) is Microsoft's directory service: centralized user/computer accounts, authentication, and Group Policy for domain members.

mcqs.prompt: A technician wants to prevent standard users from making unauthorized system changes when an installer runs. Which Windows feature prompts for administrator approval?
mcqs.context: Standard users must be prompted before system changes.

options.rationale: UAC prompts for admin approval when programs attempt system changes — the control described.
Device Manager manages drivers, not elevation prompts.
Event Viewer logs events.
msconfig configures boot/startup options.

mcqs.explanation: UAC requires confirmation (or an admin credential) before elevated actions, protecting against silent system changes. Standard users must supply an admin password at the prompt.

mcqs.prompt: A technician is asked to select the MOST secure wireless encryption for a new office access point. All client devices support the latest standard. Which option should be selected?
mcqs.context: The strongest wireless encryption supported by all clients is needed.

options.rationale: WPA3 (SAE) is the strongest wireless encryption, resistant to offline dictionary attacks — the correct choice.
WPA2 is strong but predates WPA3's SAE improvements.
WPA uses TKIP, which is deprecated and weak.
WEP is broken and must never be used.

mcqs.explanation: WPA3 (Wi-Fi Protected Access 3, using SAE) is the strongest available standard. Order: WPA3 > WPA2 > WPA > WEP.

mcqs.prompt: A company requires employees to authenticate with a username and password against a central RADIUS server before joining the corporate Wi-Fi. Which authentication framework enables this?
mcqs.context: Wi-Fi access requires centralized RADIUS authentication.

options.rationale: 802.1X is the port-based authentication framework that uses RADIUS and EAP for enterprise Wi-Fi.
Personal mode uses a shared passphrase, not per-user RADIUS authentication.
MAC filtering allows/denies by MAC address and is spoofable, not an authentication framework.
A captive portal is a web login page, not RADIUS-based 802.1X.

mcqs.explanation: 802.1X (WPA2/WPA3-Enterprise) authenticates each user via RADIUS and EAP before granting network access. Personal mode uses a single shared key; MAC filtering is not authentication.

mcqs.prompt: A user's PC is suddenly slow, shows unfamiliar pop-ups, and the browser homepage changed without permission. Which type of malware is MOST likely present?
mcqs.context: Slow PC, pop-ups, and a changed browser homepage suggest unwanted software.

options.rationale: Pop-ups plus a hijacked homepage point to adware or a potentially unwanted program (PUP) bundled with other software.
Rootkits hide deep in the OS; they do not typically produce pop-ups.
Worms self-propagate across networks; the symptoms here are adware-style.
Ransomware encrypts files and demands payment; no encryption is mentioned.

mcqs.explanation: Adware/PUPs cause pop-ups, homepage hijacking, and slowdowns — often bundled with free software. Rootkits, worms, and ransomware have different signatures.

mcqs.prompt: An endpoint security tool monitors process behavior and can automatically isolate a workstation that exhibits ransomware-like activity. Which class of tool provides this?
mcqs.context: A tool monitors behavior and isolates endpoints on ransomware-like activity.

options.rationale: EDR monitors endpoint behavior, detects threats, and can contain/isolate systems — the described capability.
Signature AV matches known file signatures; it lacks behavioral isolation.
A sniffer captures traffic; it does not isolate endpoints.
Backups restore data; they do not detect or contain threats.

mcqs.explanation: EDR uses behavioral monitoring and automated response (isolation, rollback) against threats like ransomware. Signature AV only matches known malware.

mcqs.prompt: An employee receives an urgent email from their 'bank' asking them to verify account details by clicking a link. The sender address is a free webmail account. Which attack is this?
mcqs.context: An urgent fake bank email asks for account verification via a link.

options.rationale: Phishing is a mass email impersonating a trusted entity to steal credentials — the free-webmail sender is a tell.
Whaling targets executives specifically; this is a generic bank phishing email.
Vishing is voice phishing over the phone.
Smishing is phishing via SMS text messages.

mcqs.explanation: Phishing = fraudulent email impersonating a trusted entity (bank, vendor) to harvest credentials. Whaling targets executives; vishing/smishing use voice/SMS.

mcqs.prompt: An attacker leaves USB flash drives labeled 'Executive Bonuses 2026' in a company parking lot, hoping employees plug them in. Which social engineering technique is being used?
mcqs.context: Tempting USB drives are planted to lure employees into plugging them in.

options.rationale: Baiting uses a tempting lure (like a labeled USB drive) to trigger an action — exactly this scenario.
Tailgating is following someone through a secured door.
Pretexting uses a fabricated story to gain information.
Impersonation poses as someone else; the USB lure is baiting.

mcqs.explanation: Baiting offers a physical or digital lure (USB drop, free gift) to get victims to act. Tailgating, pretexting, and impersonation are different techniques.

mcqs.prompt: A user follows a link in an email and lands on a website that looks exactly like their company's login page, but the URL is misspelled. Which TWO techniques are combined in this attack?
mcqs.context: A lookalike login page at a misspelled URL after an email link.

options.rationale: The email link is phishing — luring the user to a fake site.
The misspelled lookalike domain is typosquatting (URL hijacking).
Shoulder surfing is watching someone type credentials.
Dumpster diving retrieves discarded documents.
Tailgating follows someone through a door.

mcqs.explanation: The attack combines phishing (luring via email) with typosquatting (a misspelled lookalike domain) to harvest credentials. The other options are unrelated techniques.

mcqs.prompt: A technician is starting the malware removal process on an infected SOHO workstation. What should be done FIRST, before any scanning begins?
mcqs.context: Malware removal is starting on an infected SOHO workstation.

options.text: Investigate and verify the malware symptoms
options.rationale: The process starts by investigating and verifying symptoms, then quarantining the system.
Reimaging comes late in the process, only if removal fails.
System Restore is DISABLED during removal (so malware cannot restore itself) and re-enabled at the end.
Updating anti-malware comes AFTER quarantine and remediation steps in the official order.

mcqs.explanation: The official SOHO malware removal order: 1 investigate/verify symptoms, 2 quarantine, 3 disable System Restore, 4 remediate, 5 update anti-malware, 6 scan/remove, 7 reimage if needed, 8 schedule scans, 9 re-enable System Restore + educate.

mcqs.prompt: During malware removal, the technician disables System Restore on the infected Windows PC. Why is this done?
mcqs.context: System Restore is disabled during malware removal.

options.text: To prevent malware from restoring itself from restore points
options.rationale: Malware can hide in restore points and reappear after removal — disabling System Restore prevents that.

options.text: To free disk space for the scan
options.rationale: Disk space is not the reason; restore points are disabled to break persistence.

options.text: To speed up the antivirus scan
options.rationale: Scan speed is not affected by restore points.

options.text: To allow Windows Update to run
options.rationale: Updates are unrelated to System Restore being disabled.

mcqs.explanation: System Restore is disabled early in the removal process so malware hidden in restore points cannot restore itself; it is re-enabled and a fresh restore point created at the end.

mcqs.prompt: A security policy requires workstations to lock after 5 minutes of inactivity. Which TWO mechanisms can enforce this policy?
mcqs.context: Workstations must lock after 5 idle minutes; enforcement mechanisms are needed.

options.text: Screen lock timeout in power settings
options.rationale: The screen lock timeout setting locks the session after the configured idle time.

options.text: Group Policy security setting for interactive logon
options.rationale: Group Policy can enforce the machine inactivity limit across domain computers.
Account lockout triggers on failed logins, not inactivity.
Expiration disables accounts on a date; unrelated to idle locking.
Disabling guest removes an access path; it does not lock idle sessions.

mcqs.explanation: Screen lock timeout (power settings) and the Group Policy interactive-logon machine inactivity limit both enforce idle locking. Lockout, expiration, and guest disabling address other controls.

mcqs.prompt: A technician hardens a new workstation. Which TWO actions reduce the attack surface for autorun-based malware?
mcqs.context: Workstation hardening against autorun malware.

options.rationale: Disabling AutoRun/AutoPlay stops removable media from launching programs automatically.
Renaming/renaming the admin account is good hardening but does not stop autorun.
Login-time restrictions limit when accounts can log in, not autorun.
Disabling guest removes an access path, not autorun.
Scanning USB media before use catches malware that autorun would otherwise launch.

mcqs.explanation: Disabling AutoRun/AutoPlay and scanning removable media directly address autorun-based malware. Admin account changes and guest disabling are separate hardening steps.

mcqs.prompt: An employee's phone was jailbroken and now runs apps from unknown sources. What is the primary security implication?
mcqs.context: A jailbroken phone runs apps from unknown sources.

options.text: OS security protections have been bypassed
options.rationale: Jailbreaking/rooting removes OS security controls (code signing, sandboxing), so the device cannot be trusted.
Jailbreaking has no effect on charging speed.

options.text: The device is fully protected by the jailbreak
options.rationale: Jailbreaking reduces security; it does not protect.
Jailbroken devices can evade MDM controls; many MDMs flag them as non-compliant.

mcqs.explanation: Jailbreaking/rooting bypasses the OS security model (code signing, sandboxing, app store controls), allowing malware and making the device untrusted for corporate data.

mcqs.prompt: A company wants to enforce a passcode, remote wipe capability, and app restrictions on employee-owned phones used for work. Which technology provides centralized policy enforcement?
mcqs.context: Policy enforcement on employee-owned mobile devices.

options.rationale: MDM enrolls devices and enforces passcode, remote wipe, and app policies centrally — the described capability.
Biometrics authenticate users; they do not enforce device policy.
A captive portal gates Wi-Fi access with a login page.
A VPN encrypts traffic; it does not enforce device policies.

mcqs.explanation: MDM (mobile device management) centrally enforces passcodes, remote wipe/lock, app restrictions, and compliance on enrolled devices — including BYOD via containers.

mcqs.prompt: A company must dispose of magnetic hard drives that contained confidential data. Which destruction method is MOST appropriate for HDDs?
mcqs.context: Magnetic HDDs with confidential data must be destroyed.

options.rationale: Degaussing destroys the magnetic field and shredding physically destroys HDDs — both are appropriate for magnetic media.
Secure erase works but degaussing/shredding is the stronger physical guarantee for disposal.
Factory reset is for mobile devices, not HDDs.
Deleting files leaves recoverable data on the platters.

mcqs.explanation: Magnetic HDDs are destroyed by degaussing (wiping the magnetic field) or physical shredding. File deletion leaves recoverable data; factory reset is for mobile devices.

mcqs.prompt: A technician must securely dispose of a solid-state drive (SSD). Which method is MOST effective for SSDs?
mcqs.context: An SSD must be securely erased before disposal.

options.text: Secure erase / crypto-shred (destroy the encryption keys)
options.rationale: SSDs need secure erase or crypto-shred because degaussing does not affect flash memory and data may persist in wear-leveled cells.
Degaussing is ineffective on flash-based SSDs.
Formatting does not reliably erase SSD cells; data may remain.
Deleting files leaves recoverable data.

mcqs.explanation: SSDs require secure erase (ATA secure erase) or crypto-shred (destroying the encryption key makes data unrecoverable). Degaussing only affects magnetic media.

mcqs.prompt: A technician configures a SOHO wireless router for the first time. Which action should be taken FIRST for security?
mcqs.context: A new SOHO router needs its first security configuration.

options.rationale: Changing the default admin password is the first hardening step — default credentials are a known entry point.
Hiding the SSID is weak security theater; the admin password comes first.
MAC filtering is spoofable and secondary to credential changes.
Port forwarding EXPOSES services; it is not a first-step hardening action.

mcqs.explanation: The first SOHO router hardening step is changing the default administrator password, followed by WPA2/WPA3, firmware updates, and disabling WPS. SSID hiding and MAC filtering are weak controls.

mcqs.prompt: A SOHO router supports WPS. A security review recommends disabling it. Why?
mcqs.context: WPS should be disabled on a SOHO router.

options.text: WPS PINs are vulnerable to brute-force attacks
options.rationale: WPS's PIN method can be brute-forced (8-digit PIN, ~11,000 effective combinations), letting attackers recover the passphrase.
WPS is a setup convenience, not a speed feature.
WPA3 does not require WPS.
WPS does not block guest networks.

mcqs.explanation: WPS (Wi-Fi Protected Setup) PIN mode is vulnerable to offline brute-force attacks that reveal the network passphrase — disabling it is standard hardening.

mcqs.prompt: A user reports that their browser homepage and search engine changed without their consent after installing a free utility. Which browser security action should be taken?
mcqs.context: A browser was hijacked after a free utility install.

options.text: Reset browser settings and remove suspicious extensions
options.rationale: Browser hijacking is fixed by removing malicious extensions and resetting settings (homepage/search).
Zoom affects display size, not hijacking.
Cache clearing does not remove the hijacker or its extension.
Disabling JavaScript is drastic and does not remove the hijacking extension.

mcqs.explanation: Browser hijackers install extensions and change settings; resetting the browser and removing suspicious extensions restores control. Cache clearing alone is insufficient.

mcqs.prompt: A user wants to browse without the browser storing history, cookies, or site data after the session. Which browser feature provides this?
mcqs.context: Browsing should leave no history or site data behind.

options.rationale: Private browsing does not persist history, cookies, or site data after the session closes.
A larger cache stores MORE site data.
Pop-up blockers are unrelated to history persistence.
Autofill stores form data; it does not clear session data.

mcqs.explanation: Private/incognito mode discards history, cookies, and site data at session end. Cache growth, pop-up blockers, and autofill do the opposite or are unrelated.

mcqs.prompt: A user's browser displays a certificate warning on a trusted website. Which browser security mechanism is alerting them?
mcqs.context: A browser certificate warning appears for a trusted site.

options.rationale: Browsers validate TLS certificates; a warning means the certificate is invalid, expired, or mismatched.
Pop-up blockers stop pop-ups, not certificate warnings.
Autofill fills credentials; it does not validate certificates.
Incognito mode does not change certificate validation.

mcqs.explanation: Certificate warnings come from TLS validation — the server's certificate failed checks (expired, untrusted CA, name mismatch). Users should not bypass the warning.

mcqs.prompt: An organization issues smart cards to employees for building access and computer login. Which TWO authentication factors does a smart card combine?
mcqs.context: Smart cards are used for building and computer access.

options.rationale: The physical card is a possession factor.
Smart cards require a PIN, adding a knowledge factor.
The card/PIN combination does not include biometrics.
Location is not part of smart-card authentication.
Behavioral factors are not part of smart-card auth.

mcqs.explanation: Smart-card authentication combines possession (the card) with knowledge (the PIN) — two different factors, hence multifactor. Biometrics and location are not involved.

mcqs.prompt: Malware encrypts a user's documents and displays a message demanding payment in cryptocurrency to restore them. Which type of malware is this?
mcqs.context: Files are encrypted and payment is demanded.

options.rationale: Ransomware encrypts data and demands payment — exactly the described behavior.
Spyware secretly monitors activity; it does not encrypt files.
A logic bomb triggers on a condition; it is not typically a file-encrypting extortion tool.
Adware shows ads; it does not encrypt files.

mcqs.explanation: Ransomware encrypts victim data and demands payment (usually cryptocurrency). The correct response: isolate, report, and restore from backups — never pay.

mcqs.prompt: An attacker calls the help desk pretending to be a remote employee and asks for a password reset. Which social engineering technique is being used?
mcqs.context: An attacker impersonates a remote employee to get a password reset.

options.rationale: Pretexting uses a fabricated scenario (the 'remote employee') to obtain information or actions — the described attack.
Baiting uses a lure; no lure is involved here.
Phishing is email-based; this is a phone call.
Shoulder surfing observes credentials being typed.

mcqs.explanation: Pretexting invents a believable scenario to manipulate the target into providing access or information. Phone-based pretexting against help desks is common (also called vishing when phone-phishing).

mcqs.prompt: A technician finishes removing malware from a SOHO workstation. Which step completes the process?
mcqs.context: Malware removal is finishing on a SOHO workstation.

options.text: Enable System Restore, create a restore point, and educate the end user
options.rationale: The process ends by re-enabling System Restore, creating a clean restore point, and educating the user.

options.text: Disable the antivirus to improve performance
options.rationale: Antivirus stays enabled; disabling it invites re-infection.
Restore points are re-enabled and a fresh one created, not deleted.
Formatting is unnecessary when removal succeeded.

mcqs.explanation: The final malware-removal step re-enables System Restore (disabled earlier), creates a clean restore point, and educates the user to prevent recurrence.

mcqs.prompt: A workstation security policy requires password history and minimum length. Which tool enforces these password policies on a domain-joined Windows PC?
mcqs.context: Password history and length policies must be enforced on domain PCs.

options.rationale: Group Policy enforces password length, history, complexity, and age centrally on domain members.
BitLocker encrypts drives; it does not set password policies.
Device Manager manages drivers.
Disk Management handles partitions.

mcqs.explanation: Group Policy (Security Settings > Account Policies > Password Policy) enforces minimum length, history, complexity, and age domain-wide.

mcqs.prompt: A technician configures a corporate-owned tablet so it can ONLY install apps approved by the company and cannot change critical settings. Which mobile security approach is this?
mcqs.context: A corporate tablet is restricted to approved apps and locked settings.

options.rationale: MDM app allow-listing restricts installation to approved apps and locks settings — the described control.
Jailbreaking REMOVES restrictions; it does not enforce them.
A captive portal gates Wi-Fi login, not app installs.
MAC filtering controls network access by MAC, not apps.

mcqs.explanation: MDM app allow-listing and configuration profiles restrict a managed device to approved apps and enforce settings — standard corporate-owned device hardening.

mcqs.prompt: A technician must dispose of documents containing customer names and account numbers. Which disposal method is appropriate for paper records?
mcqs.context: Sensitive paper documents must be disposed of.

options.rationale: Cross-cut shredding destroys paper records into small pieces — the appropriate physical method.
Degaussing affects magnetic media, not paper.
Secure erase applies to digital storage.
Factory reset is for mobile devices.

mcqs.explanation: Paper records are destroyed by cross-cut shredding (or incineration). Degaussing, secure erase, and factory reset apply to electronic media.

mcqs.prompt: A small office router has been running the factory firmware for years. Which security action is MOST important for the router?
mcqs.context: A SOHO router runs old factory firmware.

options.text: Update the firmware to the latest vendor release
options.rationale: Firmware updates patch known vulnerabilities — the most important action for an aging router.
SSID hiding is weak security compared to patching known firmware flaws.
MAC filtering is spoofable and secondary to firmware patching.

options.text: Open port forwarding for the cameras
options.rationale: Port forwarding increases exposure.

mcqs.explanation: Updating router firmware patches known vulnerabilities (the top SOHO hardening item). SSID hiding and MAC filtering are weak controls; port forwarding increases exposure.

mcqs.prompt: A company must dispose of optical discs that contain an old client database. Which method is appropriate for destroying optical media?
mcqs.context: Optical discs with a client database must be destroyed.

options.rationale: Shredding physically destroys optical discs — the appropriate disposal method for CDs/DVDs.
Degaussing affects magnetic media; optical discs store data as pits, not magnetic fields.
Secure erase applies to flash/SSD storage, not optical discs.
Factory reset is for mobile devices.

mcqs.explanation: Optical discs are destroyed by physical shredding or incineration. Degaussing and secure erase do not apply to optical media; factory reset is for mobile devices.

mcqs.prompt: A technician has removed malware from a SOHO workstation. Which step should be taken to prevent recurrence and keep the system protected going forward?
mcqs.context: Malware removal succeeded; ongoing protection is needed.

options.text: Schedule scans and run updates regularly
options.rationale: Scheduled scans and regular updates maintain protection — the follow-up step in the removal process.
Disabling protection invites re-infection.
Removing the scanner removes protection.
Updates patch vulnerabilities; disabling them increases risk.

mcqs.explanation: After removal: schedule scans, keep anti-malware and OS updates current, and educate the user — the ongoing-protection steps that close the process.

mcqs.prompt: A technician compares WPA2 and WPA3 for a new wireless deployment. Which TWO advantages does WPA3 provide over WPA2?
mcqs.context: WPA3's advantages over WPA2 are being compared.

options.rationale: WPA3's SAE handshake resists offline dictionary attacks — a key improvement over WPA2's PSK.
WPA3 provides forward secrecy, so captured traffic cannot be decrypted later if the passphrase leaks.
WPA3 never uses WEP; WEP is broken.

options.text: It requires no passphrase at all
options.rationale: Personal mode still uses a passphrase; enterprise uses 802.1X.

options.text: It is faster than any wired connection
options.rationale: Wireless speed is unrelated to the security standard.

mcqs.explanation: WPA3 (SAE) resists offline dictionary attacks and provides forward secrecy. WEP compatibility and passphrase-free claims are false; speed is not a security-standard property.

mcqs.prompt: An antivirus scan flags a file that appears legitimate to the user. The file was downloaded from a well-known software vendor's site. What is the MOST likely explanation?
mcqs.context: A legitimate-looking file is flagged by antivirus.

options.rationale: Antivirus sometimes flags legitimate files (false positives), especially for heuristic or behavioral detection.
Flags can be false positives; verification is needed before assuming malware.
A single flag does not mean the AV is broken.

options.text: The file must be deleted immediately
options.rationale: Deleting a false-positive file harms the user; verify first (upload to VirusTotal or check the vendor).

mcqs.explanation: Heuristic/behavioral detection can produce false positives on legitimate files. Verify the file's hash/source before acting; do not blindly delete or trust.

mcqs.prompt: A technician applies a security baseline to a Windows workstation. Which TWO settings are part of standard workstation hardening?
mcqs.context: Standard Windows workstation hardening settings are being applied.

options.rationale: Disabling the guest account removes an unauthenticated access path — standard hardening.
Account lockout after failed attempts blocks brute-force login attempts.
AutoPlay should be DISABLED, not enabled — it is a malware vector.
Administrator for everyone violates least privilege.
The firewall should stay enabled.

mcqs.explanation: Hardening includes disabling the guest account and enabling account lockout. AutoPlay should be off, users should be standard (least privilege), and the firewall stays on.

mcqs.prompt: An employee lost their company smartphone, which contains work email and client contacts. Which mobile security capability lets the administrator protect the data on the lost device?
mcqs.context: A lost company smartphone holds work email and contacts.

options.text: Remote lock and wipe via MDM
options.rationale: MDM remote lock/wipe protects data on a lost or stolen device — the standard response.
Brightness is a display setting, not a security control.
Bluetooth pairing connects peripherals; unrelated to data protection.
A captive portal gates Wi-Fi access; it cannot wipe a lost phone.

mcqs.explanation: MDM provides remote lock and remote wipe, protecting corporate data on lost/stolen devices. Brightness, Bluetooth, and captive portals are unrelated.
